78.note_body: Egypt sees Sarai as something to acquire; Jesus calls us to examine the desire behind that gaze. God's love teaches us to honor a person's dignity, never to treat someone as a possession.

130.note_body: Isaac bound on the wood is never permission to harm a child. Read alongside the arrest of Jesus, the binding points toward the Son who freely gives Himself. The Father's provision, not human violence, carries the story forward.
130.lens_gloss: to bind - the rare, weighty verb behind Akedah, the binding of Isaac, the son Abraham dearly loved.

140.note_body: On Moriah God stopped Abraham's hand and provided a ram. At Calvary the Father gave His own Son for us. The comparison leads us to receive God's costly love; it never gives us permission to put another person in danger.
140.lens_gloss: your only one - a singular, irreplaceable son; the word names how deeply Abraham treasures Isaac.

153.lens_gloss: to set apart as holy - consecration prepares God's people to draw near with reverence.

165.note_body: Job says that God passes by unseen; Jacob wakes to discover that the Lord was present in a place he had not recognized. We may need to look back before we can name the care that was already with us.

172.note_body: Abram falls on his face as God speaks the covenant. Jesus also falls on His face in Gethsemane and brings His anguish to the Father. Reverence makes room for honest prayer when obedience is costly.

179.note_body: Famine sends Abram toward Egypt and Naomi toward Moab. Their journeys are different, yet neither road places God's promise beyond His reach. Scarcity can change an address without erasing the people God has called.

186.lens_gloss: to hear and heed - listening that leads to obedience; the same summons opens Israel's central confession, the Shema.

287.note_body: Moses calls Israel to do what is right and good in God's sight. Jesus lives that devotion, doing what pleases the Father and knowing His presence. Obedience grows from a relationship of trust, not a performance to purchase affection.

313.lens_gloss: to hear - in Hebrew, hearing can include responding obediently; God's people listen with a willingness to act.

25.note_body: The Song describes a lover knocking and a delayed response. Revelation's invitation is addressed to a church: Christ stands ready to share a meal. The passages invite attentive response, while their different settings help us hear each one clearly.

83.note_body: Joseph's brothers conspire against the son their father loves; the tenants plot against the owner's heir. Both stories expose envy that treats a person as an obstacle. Jesus calls us away from that grasping heart and toward faithful stewardship.

160.note_body: Moses tells Israel to hear the Prophet God will raise up. At the transfiguration, with Moses present, the Father's command directs the disciples to listen to Jesus. Following Him begins with giving His words our attention.

241.note_body: Matthew applies Isaiah's picture of God's chosen Servant to Jesus; Peter recalls the Father's delight declared on the holy mountain. The Father affirms the Son, and the Son serves faithfully. Service flows from that relationship, not a struggle to manufacture worth.
241.lens_gloss: dearly loved - the Father's delight in His chosen Servant; the word describes love, not a reward for productivity.

257.lens_gloss: dearly loved - the word names the father's affection for the son he sends last; compare the Father's affirmation of Jesus at His baptism.

2.lens_gloss: to call, to name - God gives Adam a real part in naming the creatures He has made.

96.note_body: Samson stakes garments on a contest before his companions. Jesus enters His ministry with the Father's affirmation already spoken over Him. Those different scenes help us ask whether we are acting from secure belonging or trying to win our worth from a crowd.

114.lens_gloss: to be anxious, to care - the concern in this scene moves from missing donkeys to a much-loved son.

155.lens_gloss: dearly loved - the Father's cherished Servant, whose work expresses His relationship with the Father.
